Current evidence supports Dutch and Italian instruction; translated English titles are not treated as English teaching evidence.

alternatives.label: Italy, Europe & the Mediterranean: history, politics & culture
alternatives.concept: Study modern Italy through European and Mediterranean history, comparative politics, international relations, national identity, sociology, art, film and cultural research. This is a related humanities and social-science route; it preserves the absence of Italian-language proficiency and a cumulative Italy-specific disciplinary sequence.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines modern European and Mediterranean history, politics, sociology, Renaissance Italy, art-historical research, literature, film and media. The label names Italy as the motivating case without presenting the route as Italian Language and Culture or Italian-language training.
progression: The schedule contains 24 unique courses / 180 EC, four courses per semester, Personal & Professional Development in Year 1 and eleven level-300 courses. Every course is available in its assigned Fall-2026-start term and none has a formal prerequisite. Introductory history, politics, sociology, Mediterranean art history, literature and film precede advanced EU politics, archival research, conflict, social theory, persuasion, literary-film, media and art-historical research. No Italian-language prerequisite or proficiency is implied.

alternatives.label: Literature, media & cultural identity
alternatives.concept: Study how literary, rhetorical, linguistic, artistic and media forms create cultural meaning and express identity and power, combining textual interpretation, psycholinguistics, intercultural communication, Renaissance Italy, film and multimodal production. Preserve Italian-language acquisition, Italian linguistics, translation and sustained Italy-specific depth as explicit gaps.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed route concentrates on literature, stylistics, rhetoric, psycholinguistics, Renaissance Italy, film, media and cultural identity; it does not claim Italian proficiency or a full Italian Studies curriculum.
progression: The schedule contains 24 unique courses / 180 EC, four courses per semester, Personal & Professional Development in Year 1 and seven level-300 courses. Every course is available in its assigned Fall-2026-start term; Introduction to Brain & Behavior precedes Psycholinguistics by four semesters. Introductory literature, rhetoric, sociology, film/media and Renaissance Italy precede advanced persuasive, creative and interpretive work. No Italian-language competence is implied.
alternatives.distinctness: Ten courses / 75 EC differ in each direction. Comparative politics, international relations, modern sociology, EU politics, historical research, peace and conflict, Western military history, documentary study and art-historical research are replaced by literary studies, rhetoric, psycholinguistics, media archaeology, life writing, popular media and community communication. The change shifts the programme from Italy in European and Mediterranean historical-political context to language, literature and mediated cultural identity.

candidates.label: Italian proficiency, linguistics, translation and Italian-language writing

selection.assessment: Two complete related-field programmes pass the evidence, course-content, schedule and pairwise 30-EC distinctness gates. The first studies Italy through European and Mediterranean history, politics, society, identity, art and cultural research; the second develops literature, rhetoric, psycholinguistics, film, media and cultural identity. A third Italian-proficiency and linguistics programme is not feasible because the current workbook contains no Italian acquisition sequence, Italian grammar, sociolinguistics, translation or Italian-language academic writing. Psycholinguistics and stylistics contribute genuine language study but cannot be expanded into or labelled as Italian proficiency.

notes.text: The UCR alternatives study modern European and Mediterranean history, Italian Renaissance art, politics, national identity, sociology, literature, film, media, rhetoric, psycholinguistics and cultural research. UCR does not offer Italian proficiency progression, Italian grammar and sociolinguistics, translation, Italian-language academic work or the compulsory semester in Italy, so these are related humanities and social-science routes rather than Italian Language and Culture equivalents.
